slides.headline: His food initiative fed 30 million people during COVID. In 2026, TIME named him one of the 100 most influential people alive.
Chef Vikas Khanna's Feed India initiative delivered over 30 million meals across 135 cities during the pandemic.
slides.body: Long before the recognition, Khanna - an 8-Michelin-star chef - redirected his career toward large-scale food relief, running the effort alongside his culinary and filmmaking work rather than as a side project.

slides.headline: TIME named him to its 2026 TIME100 list - the first Indian culinary figure ever included.
slides.body: He joins the list alongside fellow honorees Sundar Pichai and Ranbir Kapoor, recognized for a body of work that spans his humanitarian food-relief work, his directorial debut 'The Last Color,' and his Cannes-premiered documentary 'Kitchens of Gratitude.'

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat needs its most visible global figures to still show up for the basics.
slides.body: Khanna's recognition came from a decade of feeding people, not just cooking for them - a reminder that global influence and grassroots relief work aren't opposites.
